text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx + queue latency on /v1/chat/stream (hosted-prod-us-east). 5m window: errors=14%, p95=1.5s, backlog growth on schedulers.

sam_oncall: ack — I'm paged. Tailing logs and runtime metrics.

rachel_sre: joining. Initial glance: lots of sub-100-token requests, many single-turn calls. Continuous batching trace shows high churn: many batches of size 1-2. GPU kernel overhead and context-switching killing throughput.

sam_oncall: can we try enlarging coalescing window to pack more into each batch? That will increase tail latency but should reduce 5xxs. Also we should try disabling streaming (WS chunked) for noisy keys as a faster mitigation, less kernel flushes.

luis_prod: note — disabling streaming impacts some customers expecting progressive tokens. Need CS aware. If we throttle or disable for specific API keys, we can preserve experience for others.

rachel_sre: propose canary on shard gpx-07: set continuous_batching.coalesce_ms 12 -> 70, continuous_batching.min_batch_tokens 8 -> 64, enable pack_by_tokens=true. And mark streaming_disabled_for_keys=[key_zzz,key_abc] for noisy tenants.

sam_oncall: also propose soft per-key burst limit for top offenders: reduce burst window from 200->50 for top 5 keys. That buys relief while we roll.

rachel_sre: executing canary now on gpx-07. Command:

```bash
redwoodctl runtime update --shard gpx-07 \
  --set continuous_batching.coalesce_ms=70 \
  --set continuous_batching.min_batch_tokens=64 \
  --set continuous_batching.pack_by_tokens=true
```

deploy-bot: update started on gpx-07 by rachel_sre at 1923456832.

sam_oncall: applying streaming toggle for noisy keys (canary list) via config push.

```json
{"action":"patch_keys","disable_streaming":["key_zzz","key_abc"],"effective":"now"}
```

deploy-bot: streaming toggle applied at 1923456850.

sam_oncall: metrics after ~2m on gpx-07: errors from 14% -> 6.8%, batch size median from 2 -> 9, p95 on gpx-07 increased from 1.5s -> 1.85s, but cluster error rate trending down. GPU mem/OOMs unchanged.

luis_prod: customer impact note: Emma/CS to prepare targeted comms for keys in disable list. Also status page draft: "We've applied targeted backend batching optimizations and streaming toggles to improve reliability; some customers may see slightly higher end-to-end latency."

emma_cs: acknowledging. I'll message affected customers and add playbook entries.

rachel_sre: canary stable for 7m with error rate halved. Proceeding to rollout to remaining us-east shards (gpx-01,gpx-02,gpx-03) with 60s stagger and per-shard validation.

```bash
for shard in gpx-01 gpx-02 gpx-03; do
  redwoodctl runtime update --shard $shard \
    --set continuous_batching.coalesce_ms=70 \
    --set continuous_batching.min_batch_tokens=64 \
    --set continuous_batching.pack_by_tokens=true &
  sleep 60
done
```

deploy-bot: gpx-01 success at 1923456955. gpx-02 success at 1923457018. gpx-03 success at 1923457060.

sam_oncall: cluster-wide errors down to 3.0%. median batch sizes up, scheduler churn reduced. Aggregate p95 across region ~1.6s (was 1.5s pre-incident), p50 stable. Small-request latency increased slightly but success rates improved.

luis_prod: agreed to keep changes for 3 hours while we root cause. Also request: please add an automated routing rule to prefer larger-pack shards for noisy short-request keys.
\rachel_sre: created follow-up ticket INF-4332: "Investigate short-request surge & implement latency-aware adaptive batching + per-key streaming opt-out". Assign to eng-runtime with priority P2.

emma_cs: posted targeted messages to affected customers and updated status page: "Mitigation in place; monitoring. Expect slight latency increase for small requests."

sam_oncall: other mitigations we applied: temporary per-key burst caps for top 5 noisy keys (reduced to 40r/min), streaming disabled for 2 keys, and batching coalescing across region increased. If we see p95 climb above 2.5s, revert streaming toggle for all keys and re-evaluate.

rachel_sre: leaving a concrete rollback and escalation plan in the thread for next oncall: 1) revert batching coalesce to 12ms (fast rollback via redwoodctl), 2) re-enable streaming for keys if customer-impacted, 3) apply temporary global throttle (15%) if errors reappear.

sam_oncall: handing off at 1923457150 to night oncall. Current status: mitigations live, cluster error rate stable at 3.0%, tail latency elevated but within acceptable emergency SLO.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated (ongoing monitor). Summary: increased batching coalescing and min batch tokens + disabled streaming for noisy keys -> error rate improved from 14% to 3%, tradeoff is ~100-350ms added tail latency.

emma_cs: thanks all. CS will follow up on customer questions and track any escalations. :white_check_mark:
